decisions.quote:
First, our result gives some credence to the ﬁndings of Stelzl et al. (2008). In

fact, we found a marginally signiﬁcant interaction, and a signiﬁcant interaction

between team identity and tournament outcome. We found that, following a

positive outcome, participants were more likely to highlight the judoka’s in-
group French identity (H1) and to perceive themselves as similar to the athlete

(H2). As in prior research, those effects appeared only when participants shared

Bernache-Assollant et al. 9

an identity with the athlete.
decisions.location: Independent parent reading of exact primary Methods/Discussion and original-specific context; raw contiguous extraction retained
decisions.reason: Original-specific Discussion confirms both nationality and self-similarity MOATing comparisons and says their restriction to shared identity matches prior research. The abstract governs with generally-replicate wording; the new stereotype outcome and self-enhancement-versus-protection interpretation are extensions. A marginal omnibus nationality interaction does not override the authors interpretation of the original contrast and whole replication. Same DOI confirms online2007/issue2008 identity, rather than two originals.
